question.text: This modern-day Balkan country staged a decades-long revolt against Ottoman rule in the 15th century led by Skanderbeg. In the 20th century, it was ruled by the dictator Enver Hoxha (HOE-juh).
question.clue: Its southern boundary is formed by the Pindus Mountains and its longest river is the Drin, which empties in the north.

swap.leadin: Its source is in the Black Forest region of Germany.
swap.text: Name this river that flows through Vienna long before it reaches the Black Sea.
swap.clue: This river was partly responsible for the 2006 European floods and was subjected to a red toxic sludge spill in 2010.

question.text: This former Yugoslav President was tried for war crimes at The Hague, but died in prison in of a heart attack in 2006 while still awaiting a verdict.
question.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

swap.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
swap.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
swap.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

question.text: After several failed attempts to assassinate Franz Ferdinand, this nineteen year old eventually shot both Ferdinand and his wife, Sophie.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.leadin: In 1981, a leader of this country banned typewriters because he feared citizens were using them to write messages to foreign embassies detailing the conditions in his country.
swap.text: Name this country whose dictator Nicolae Ceausescu declared contraception illegal under Decree 770 in an attempt to increase this country's population.
swap.clue: A ruler of this country embraced a "mini-Cultural Revolution" as part of a return to socialist realism in the July Theses.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the real-life Count Dracula, Vlad the Impaler.
question.text: While Vlad Dracula is commonly associated with Transylvania, he actually ruled over this region, which was combined with Transylvania and Moldavia to form the modern Romania.
question.clue: This region was the first one to be ruled by Michael the Brave.

swap.leadin: In this leader's last public appearance, people shouted "Timisoara" in reference to an uprising he had violently suppressed.
swap.text: Name this long-time Communist leader of Romania. This man and his wife's execution was nearly caught on live television following a 1989 revolution.
swap.clue: This man, who used the Securitate secret police, was the only leader subjected to a violent overthrow during the anti-Communist Revolutions of 1989.

question.text: Out With The Old Founded in the fourteenth century as Dambovita Citadel, this key city along the trade route to Constantinople became the residence of the Walachian prince. The home of the headquarters of Cominform from 1948 to 1956, much of its Old City was demolished for new buildings on a tributary of the Danube. For 15 points-name this Eastern European city.
question.clue: A coup led by this city's orthodox Metropolitan Neophyte ended its post-1848 revolutionary period.

swap.leadin: Cardinal Aloysius Stepinac was imprisoned for allegedly supporting this organization.
swap.text: Name this Nazi-aligned fascist organization led by Ante Pavelic that ruled Croatia during World War 2.
swap.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the military successes and failures of the Ottoman Empire.
question.text: The Ottoman sultan Murad II defeated the "Athlete of Christ," Janos Hunyadi, at the battle of Varna in this country. Basil II earned one of his epithets by subjugating this country.
question.clue: This country was defeated in the Second Balkan War and led by Tsar Boris III during World War II.

swap.leadin: Though famous for other reasons, this man was known as a playwright and novelist throughout his life, authoring such works as The Truth that Killed.
swap.text: Name this dissident who was assassinated in London in 1978. The murder has been traced to a secret service agent codenamed "Piccadilly", whose real identity is often suspected to be the Danish citizen Francesco Gullino.
swap.clue: This Bulgarian dissident who was infamously assassinated in 1978 when a pellet containing ricin was fired from an umbrella into his leg.

question.leadin: Franjo ("FRAHN-yo") Tudjman and Slobodan Milosevic's encouragement of "long-distance nationalism" following this agreement solidified collective legacies of ethnic cleansing, such as that at Srebrenica ("sreh-BREN-eet-suh").
question.text: Name this agreement that ended the Bosnian War by creating a power-sharing framework between the Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
question.answerHtml: Dayton Accords [or Dayton Agreement; or General Framework Agreement for Peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina]
question.clue: Richard Holbrooke served as the chief negotiator for this agreement.

swap.leadin: In response to a proposed alliance from Giovanni Antonio Orsini, this person offered his people's descent from Pyrrhus of Epirus as a refusal.
swap.text: Name this person who invaded southern Italy at the behest of Ferdinand I of Naples. This Albanian folk hero founded the League of Lezhe.
swap.clue: The Rilindja period of literary flourishment drew from that biography of this "Prince of the Epirotes" by Marin Barleti.

question.leadin: This politician launched Operation Storm, the armed takeover of the Republic of Serbian Krajina ("KRAH-ee-nah"), after it refused to adopt the Z-4 Plan for reintegration with Croatia.
question.text: Name this president of Croatia throughout most of the 1990s. He signed the Erdut Agreement with the remaining independent republics and thus fully achieved Croatian independence.
question.clue: Along with Milosevic, this neofascist Croatian dictator was party to the earlier 1995 Dayton Accords, which allowed for the NATO implementation force to take over for U.N. peacekeepers in Bosnia.

swap.leadin: Zvonimir Boban became a national hero after kicking a police officer in this city.
swap.text: Name this city, whose Maksimir Stadium was the site of riots between the Bad Blue Boys and the Delije (DEL-eye), fans of rival soccer teams. One side in those riots in this city was led by a man known as "Arkan."
swap.clue: Tuđman's ("TOODJ-man") refusal to confirm opposition candidate Goran Granic as mayor of this capital of Croatia led to its namesake crisis, during which Tuđman compared protestors to "small-time cattle."

question.leadin: Answer the following about ugly politics behind the Iron Curtain.
question.text: Together with Petru Groza, this Romanian leader reportedly held King Michael at gunpoint to convince him to abdicate. After becoming prime minister in 1952, he forged alliances with China and other non-communist states, before being succeeded as party leader by Nicolae Ceausescu ("chow-SHES-koo").
question.clue: This patron of Nicolae Ceausescu was the Communist leader of Romania from 1948 to 1965. Domestically, he emphasized the manufacturing of consumer goods, while he sought to improve foreign relations with both the West and China.

swap.leadin: Name some fields in European history which have really cool names.
swap.text: The Serbian prince Lazar was crushed at this field during the Battle of Kosovo in 1389, while Milos Obilic got some revenge by stabbing Murad I.

question.text: Tuđman launched Operation Storm and obliterated the forces of Serbian Krajina after agreeing to lend this leader military aid via the Split Agreement. With Tuđman and Slobodon Milosevic, this first President of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed the 1995 Dayton Accords.

swap.text: During World War II, this collaborationist Serbian leader of the Government of National Salvation actively promoted the Myth of Kosovo and requested the transfer of Kosovar territory to Serbia from his German suzerains.
swap.answerHtml: Milan Nedić(“neh-DITCH”) [reject “Milutin Nedić,” his brother who fought against the Germans]
swap.clue: In 1939, after Nazi Germany occupied Serbia, this man was entrusted to lead the territory and "save the core of the Serbian people."
